To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
heterozygosity of a myostatin gene mutation (g+6732G>A) and administration of ractopamine interact with the level of nutrition to influence growth and myofiber type characteristics in lambs.

the MSTN A/G genotype interacts with the level of feed intake (ad libitum or restricted) to affect growth, carcass, and muscle characteristics of lambs and that the β-agonist RAC interacts with the MSTN A allele to increase growth and muscle characteristics of lamb carcasses.

heterozygous lambs fed at high levels of nutrition and given ractopamine had the greatest growth rates and carcass composition, but lambs fed at low levels of nutrition and not given ractopanine had the poorest growth rates and composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between myostatin and nutrition in the context of growth and myofiber type characteristics.
understanding how myostatin allelic variants affect muscle growth and composition of lambs.
the interaction of nutrition, genetics, and pharmacological intervention on growth, composition, muscle characteristics, and meat quality in lambs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heterozygosity in MSTN A/G lambs increased lean growth in a high plane of nutritional background, but not in lambs with low plane of nutrition.
MSTN A/G lambs have a more positive response to RAC when they have a good nutritional background.
the myostatin A/G genotype and level of nutrition interact to affect growth, carcass characteristics, and myofibers of the LM in lambs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the myostatin allelic state interacts with level of nutrient intake to affect growth, carcass, and myofibril characteristics of lambs.

heterozygosity of the g+6723G >A myostatin mutation and the inclusion of RAC in the ration of lambs increased the growth rate, lean deposition, myofiber area of type I fibers, and myofibrer proportion of type IIC fibers in lambs.
the heterozygosity of the myostatin gene interacts with nutrition and β-adrenergics to affect growth, carcass characteristics, and myofibers of lambs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the myostatin allelic variation interacts with the plane of nutrition to influence growth, composition, myofiber area, and myofibers types of lambs.

heterozygous lambs are more responsive to RAC supplementation when they have been fed a high level of nutrition, which suggests that the heterozygosity of the myostatin gene may be a useful marker for identifying lambs that are more likely to respond to β-agonists.

myostatin heterozygous lambs have potential for greater growth and muscle deposition than wildtype lambs, but this potential is only realized when they are fed at a high plane of intake and are supplemented with a β-adrenergically acting compound.
